neighbours.label: ' some' (or ' of') introducing an activity noun after do/did in an account of what a group has been doing ("did some research", "doing some gardening")
fire: This week the class planted beans and then did some drawing of the seeds.
Over the holidays we visited Grandma and did some fishing at the lake.
After the trip to the zoo, the children did some writing about elephants.
On Tuesday our group went outside and did some measuring of the playground.
Year Two read a story together and then did some acting in the hall.
We have been doing some sewing in art club, which everyone enjoyed.
In science the pupils did some testing of magnets on different metals.
Before the concert the choir did some singing practice in the music room.
quiet: This week the class planted beans and then drew pictures of the seeds.
Over the holidays we visited Grandma and went fishing at the lake.
After the trip to the zoo, the children wrote stories about elephants.
On Tuesday our group went outside and measured the playground.
Year Two read a story together and then acted it out in the hall.
We have been sewing cushions in art club, which everyone enjoyed.
In science the pupils tested magnets on different metals.
Before the concert the choir practised their songs in the music room.
